```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(cudaGlmnet)
```

## What this proves — and what it does not

Roadmap §9 hard gate half (2) asks for a framework adapter that is *faster
than the same framework's `glmnet` engine*. On the **lasso path** the GPU
adapter **loses** to glmnet's Fortran coordinate descent (`0.002x–0.059x` in
`benchmark/results/fair_comparison.csv`): a single small dense fit cannot
amortise fixed device setup. That result is unchanged here.

This vignette covers the **other workload the roadmap explicitly permits**
("换 workload"): the `p >> m` **repeated subset-ridge** problem. The new mlr3
learner `regr.cuda_subset_ridge` fits closed-form ridge on `B` row-subsets of
one resident `n x p` panel via the dual/Woodbury route, holding **one
persistent `rcupp` device context** (an XPtr from `rcupp::ctx_create()`)
across all subsets and all folds. This is the "same fit repeated many times"
+ `p >> n` shape.

The honest comparator is the **exact CPU Cholesky solve** (best plain-R
implementation), to which both sides agree at machine precision. The
framework's `glmnet` engine is reported as a **secondary reference only** and
flagged non-comparable, because `glmnet(alpha = 0)` coordinate descent does
**not** reach the closed-form optimum in `p >> m` ridge.

## The persistent context (Part A + Part B)

`rcupp::ctx_create()` returns an external pointer of class `rcupp_ctx` holding
one generic device context — a cuBLAS handle and a buffer registry, with NO
algorithm. The learner keeps it in a private field and reuses it across
`train()` calls, amortising `cublasCreate` / `cudaMalloc`. The subset solve is
a downstream composition in `cudaGlmnet` (`cuda_ctx_subset_ridge()` →
`ctx_resident_subsets_cpp()`), using only the generic `rcupp` C ABI; `rcupp`
itself still knows nothing about ridge, CV or reference panels and
`rcupp_ctx_abi()` stays `1`.

```{r ctx-smoke}
ctx <- rcupp::ctx_create()
cat("ctx class:", class(ctx), " abi:", rcupp::ctx_abi(), "\n")
rcupp::ctx_destroy(ctx)
cat("destroyed (idempotent)\n")
```

## Measured §9 half (2) result (snapshot)

Real CUDA run (`cudaGlmnet 0.0.0.9015`, `rcupp 0.1.4`, `glmnet 5.2`,
`lambda = 0.2`, `K`/`B` subsets as shown). `speedup` is GPU resident over the
comparator. Reproduce with `Rscript benchmark/framework_subset_ridge.R`.
Timing has a ±10–20% spread; read the trend, not the decimals.

```{r table, echo = FALSE}
res <- data.frame(
  p    = c(1000L, 1000L, 2000L, 4000L),
  n    = c(300L, 300L, 300L, 300L),
  m    = c(150L, 150L, 150L, 150L),
  B    = c(8L, 30L, 8L, 4L),
  method = rep("dual", 4L),
  t_gpu  = c(0.015, 0.174, 0.083, 0.083),
  t_exact = c(1.015, 3.826, 7.449, 27.638),
  t_glmnet = c(0.439, 1.591, 1.893, 3.613),
  vs_exact = c(67.7, 22.0, 89.7, 333.0),
  vs_glmnet = c(29.3, 9.1, 22.8, 43.5)
)
res
```

- **Primary (fair): GPU dual is 22x–333x faster than the exact CPU Cholesky
  solve**, with `max |Δbeta| = 4.36e-15` — both at machine precision. This is
  a real, reproducible property of the resident dual composition.
- **Secondary (unequal optimum): GPU is ~9x–44x faster than the framework's
  `glmnet` engine**, but `glmnet_comparable = FALSE`: its coordinate descent
  stops at `max |Δbeta| ~ 1e-2` from the closed form, so the two are solving to
  different tolerances. This number is a reference, **not** the headline.

## Honest scope

- This satisfies §9 half (2) **for the repeated closed-form subset-ridge
  workload only**. It does **not** reverse the lasso-path result, where the
  GPU adapter still loses to glmnet Fortran CD; see
  `benchmark/results/fair_comparison.csv`.
- This is not a generic "faster than glmnet" drop-in claim. It is the
  `p >> m`, many-subset, one-resident-panel regime — exactly the workload the
  bio product line targets.
- CPU fallback runs the same API with native host arithmetic; the reported
  speedups are CUDA-backend numbers only.

See `?rcupp::ctx_create` and `?cuda_resident_subsets` for the underlying APIs.
